actual_cell_constraint: At an off-standard cell, the four local-basis support sets are pairwise disjoint by their actual pair-product ONBs against the corresponding standard-row products. The board-column coordinate is forbidden by each QLS column ONB, leaving at most seven axes. Hence at most one member can be heavy there: two support-at-least-three rays and the other two nonzero rays would require at least eight axes. A support-four ray forces all other three supports to be singletons; a support-three ray permits at most one support-two ray among the others.
actual_component_budget: Fix a standard-row coordinate a and a member M. On the seven nonstandard rows and seven columns other than a, the nonzero a-coefficients form the support of a doubly stochastic matrix, by the actual row and column ONBs. Every connected component has equally many rows and columns. A degree-one vertex has coefficient modulus one and is an isolated singleton component; all other components have minimum degree two and size at least two. If e_{M,a} is the edge count and sigma=e_{M,a}-7, then sigma>=0 and each nontrivial component on k rows contributes at least k to sigma. Pair-product orthogonality against the first-row cell a makes the four members' edge sets disjoint in the 7x7 board, so sum_M sigma_{M,a} <=49-4*7=21. This is the exact four-family per-axis counterpart of the stronger five-family 14-surplus budget; no transfer between the two is made.
global_identity: Summing sigma over the eight coordinates counts exactly the total off-standard-cell support surplus sum_{M,x}(|supp(M_x)|-1). Hence the four-family upper bound is 8*21=168, the same physical upper bound obtained directly by at most 3 surplus units per off-row cell.
